passage: Advisor's note. Tanuja came to my office on Wednesday, still shaking. A traffic official had fined her for a parking violation at a spot with no sign, and had brushed off her questions. Her friend Zeenat came with her. Tanuja said she wanted to go back and shout at the official until they understood how unfair it was. Her fists were tight and she kept saying, "They just don't care." I let her say it all. Then we looked at what she had: Zeenat's photos of the bare wall, the receipt, the time. I helped her write a short, plain complaint to the city office, and they filed it together that afternoon. Tanuja left less furious, with something to do. I will ask her next week what reply has come.

qa.q: Who came with Tanuja to the advisor's office?
What did Tanuja want to do before the advisor helped her?
qa.a: She wanted to go back and shout at the official, feeling furious and helpless that they didn't care.
It included Zeenat's photos of the bare wall, the receipt and the time, and it was written plainly and calmly.

qa.q: How might the official have seen the fine and Tanuja's questions?
qa.a: The official may have seen it as routine work and not as unfair, so shouting would probably have made the situation worse.

grounding: After an unfair fine the protagonist is furious and helpless; anger is turned into a calm record and a complaint instead of a confrontation.

passage:
Monday. At the Indore food street, a municipal inspector fined Pranav's momo cart for blocking the road, though his cart was inside the painted line like everyone else's. When Pranav pointed at the line, the inspector smirked and wrote a bigger number. Pranav's hands clenched. He wanted to shout every word he knew.

Jatin, from the juice cart next door, grabbed his elbow. "Don't. He wants you to."

Wednesday. Pranav was still furious, lying awake. Jatin came over with his phone: he had filmed the painted line and the inspector's number plate. They wrote down the time, the amount and exactly what was said.

Saturday. At the municipal grievance office they filed a written complaint with the photos. The clerk gave them a receipt. Three other cart owners, hearing about it, brought their own fines to add to the complaint.

qa.q: Who filmed the painted line and the inspector's number plate?
qa.a: Jatin, from the juice cart next door, filmed them.

qa.q: What was Pranav feeling when the inspector wrote a bigger number?
qa.a: Pranav felt furious and helpless, his hands clenching as he wanted to shout.

qa.q: Which choice worked better than shouting, and why?
qa.a: Recording the evidence calmly and filing a written complaint worked better, because it created a record and drew other cart owners in.

qa.q: How might the other cart owners have felt hearing about the complaint?
qa.a: They likely felt encouraged and less alone, seeing that there was a way to act on unfair fines.

grounding: The three beats show a young man furious after an unfair fine who records calmly, uses complaint channels and turns anger into action.

passage:
Himani, you're angry about that officer at the passport office? Good. Keep the anger, but listen to your Vidya aunty's story first. When I was twenty-two, going home on the night train from Delhi, a ticket checker kept coming back to my berth. He said my ticket was wrong. It wasn't. He sat too close and said I could pay him, or get off at the next station, alone, at midnight.

I wanted to scream at him. My whole body was burning. But I knew shouting might make him drag me off.

So I stood up, walked to the next compartment where a family was sitting, and asked the grandmother if I could sit with them. I wrote his badge number on my hand. In Lucknow I went straight to the station office and wrote a complaint. It took two months. He was transferred.

Anger gave me the strength. Calm gave me the win.

qa.q: Where did Vidya write the ticket checker's badge number?
qa.a: She wrote it on her hand.

qa.q: What was young Vidya feeling when the ticket checker threatened her?
qa.a: Young Vidya felt furious and frightened, wanting to scream with her whole body burning, but also helpless.

qa.q: What choice inside the story kept Vidya safe and led to action?
qa.a: Vidya moved to sit with a family, noted the badge number, and filed a written complaint at the station office.

qa.q: How might the grandmother in the next compartment have seen Vidya?
qa.a: The grandmother likely saw a young woman in trouble and felt protective, letting her sit with the family.

grounding: The elder's story shows a young woman harassed by an official who, instead of shouting, records details, finds safety and uses complaint channels.
